summary.headline: FY26 PAT rose 360.9% to INR28.49 crore on caustic soda volume up 29.7%; Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 14.03% on grid power rate hike.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of INR393.1 crore (up 44.62% YoY), PAT of INR28.49 crore and EBITDA of INR66.38 crore at a 16.89% margin. Q4 FY26 total income was INR97.75 crore (up 22.3% YoY), PAT INR4.39 crore (up 68.64%) and EBITDA INR13.72 crore at 14.03%, down from Q3's margin above 20% due to the October 2025 grid power tariff revision and an electrolyser renovation. Renewable share of power is about 15-20% now, targeted at 40-45% once the 21 MW solar plant (due mid-June 2026) and the 10 MW group captive project are fully running. The sulfuric acid project has been deferred on sulfur market volatility.

segments.name: Caustic soda (lye)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 84,690 MT (+29.7%); Q4 volume 20,935 MT (+8.72% YoY). Management says lye realisations improved QoQ, though caustic prices were still said to be 12-15% above pre-war levels after a March spike of 30-35%.

segments.name: Chlorinated paraffin wax (CPW)
segments.commentary: Contributed meaningfully to Q4 revenue per management. CPW capacity is being expanded from 50 to 100 TPD, with commissioning expected around end-FY27.

guidance_outlook: Renewable share of power to rise to 40-45% after the 21 MW solar plant (mid-June 2026) and full output from the 10 MW hybrid group captive project (by June end, per management).
Expected power headwind to ease meaningfully after solar commissioning; management expects margins to recover in coming quarters after electrolyser renovation.
Post-expansion installed capacity to be 360 TPD after decommissioning a 40 TPD plant; the 100 TPD caustic and CPW expansions are expected around end-FY27.
Capacity utilisation expected to reach 80-85% over the next year.
Long-term debt of roughly INR90 crore to be raised in addition to INR90 crore already on books; average cost of debt quoted at just under 8% (total around 7.9%).
Total capex outlay INR315 crore across FY24 to FY27-28; first phase of INR150 crore completed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and the renewable and capacity pipeline, but cautious on near-term sulfur supply and deferred the sulfuric acid project. Answers on the group captive power shortfall and renewable savings were less precise, with no solar savings figure given.
key_quotes: These numbers reflect the power of operating leverage when volume growth is combined with cost discipline.
Financial year 2026 marks an inflection point for Lords Chloro Alkali.

qa_highlights.question: Shortfall of about 97 lakh units from the group captive project: how is it accounted for, and will it reverse the power expense?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shortfall is per the share purchase and power purchase agreement after a grace period to November; wind delays and battery issues caused it. Full committed units expected from June 2026; the credit taken in power expenses is not reversible.

qa_highlights.question: With utilisation near 80% and new capacity only at end-FY27, how will growth look over the next few quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the growth cycle over the next year with utilisation of 80-85%, and says Q4 shortfall was partly due to the war situation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the sulfuric acid project not taken ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: It was meant to add a chemical line and use the heat from acid making for flaking; sulfur markets have been volatile for 6-9 months and the war began about three months ago, so it is deferred.

qa_highlights.question: Why did caustic prices spike in March and come back toward pre-war levels; is excess supply coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices rose 30-35% and are still 12-15% above pre-war levels. He sees no major shift of export capacity to domestic market; European orders are recovering after freight disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA margin fall from Q3's above 20% to about 14%?
qa_highlights.answer: The grid tariff revision from 1 October applied to both quarters; caustic prices fell somewhat from Q3 to Q4, and an electrolyser was shut for renovation (anodes, cathodes, membranes), raising power consumption. Management expects catch-up in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net renewable saving and the power cost without the 16 MW solar plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give the figure. Grid landed cost rose from about INR7 to INR8.2-8.3 per unit (15-18% discom hike); renewable share is about 15-20%, going to around 40%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of debt and interest outlook with the capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is a little under 8%, total about 7.9%. Additional long-term debt of about INR90 crore to be raised on top of about INR90 crore on books.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add renewables beyond the current capex cycle, and what is the blended power cost target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is always looking for opportunities, will assess after the 21 MW project and after the market settles on domestic cells mandated from this month. Blended cost target not quantified beyond grid at INR8.2-8.3 per unit.

capex_capacity: Total capex outlay INR315 crore across FY24 to FY27-28; first phase of INR150 crore completed (90 TPD caustic soda expansion, 16 MW Bikaner solar, equity into 10 MW hybrid group captive project).

Second phase in execution: 21 MW solar plant (Rajasthan), CPW expansion from 50 to 100 TPD, and a further 100 TPD caustic soda expansion; solar expected operational around mid-June 2026; CPW and caustic expansions expected around end-FY27.
Post-expansion installed capacity 360 TPD after decommissioning an old 40 TPD plant (would otherwise have been 400 TPD).
Renewable captive capacity to be 37 MW after 21 MW solar, plus 10 MW from group captive project; renewable share of power to reach 40-45% (currently about 15-20%).

Group captive project: 100 MW wind-solar hybrid in Jaisalmer, of which Lords contributed 10 MW; solar at 100 MW complete, wind 65 MW commissioned with full 100 MW expected next month; full committed units expected from June onwards.
Sulfuric acid project deferred due to sulfur market volatility; management says it is on a back burner under prudent capital allocation.
Capacity utilisation expected at 80-85% over the next year; North India capacity share expected to rise to 26-27% from about 20% (300 TPD of roughly 1,600 TPD regional capacity).
demand_pricing: Management cites Indian demand growth of about 5-6% overall and 4-5% in North India, with no new North India caustic capacity expected for 2-2.5 years beyond the company's own expansion; expects demand to exceed supply in the region.
Caustic soda prices spiked 30-35% in March 2026 and, per management, are now still about 12-15% above pre-war levels. Lye realisations improved QoQ in Q4.

Management said chlorine prices are negative in India; ECU (chlorine plus caustic) pricing expected to offset, and new large-scale 2 to 2.5 million tonne capacities on the West Coast are expected to export rather than flood domestic market.
Demand drivers cited: aluminium, paper, textiles, pharmaceuticals. CPW converts chlorine into a value-added downstream product.

Raw materials: salt (about 11-12% of production cost) on yearly contract, no price variation; purification chemicals up 20-25%, in some cases 30%, but only 1-2% of total cost; about 1.61-1.62 tonnes salt per tonne caustic.
risks_watch: Sulfur supply volatility: sulfuric acid project deferred and no timeline given for restart.
Execution risk on 21 MW solar (mid-June 2026 target), the 10 MW group captive project's full delivery by June end, and the domestic cell mandate that may slow panel procurement.
Caustic price normalisation: prices still said to be 12-15% above pre-war levels after a 30-35% spike; chlorine negative pricing in India.
New West Coast capacity of 2-2.5 million tonnes over three years could add supply pressure in domestic markets (management expects exports instead).
Interest cost rise with about INR90 crore of new long-term debt; capacity utilisation target of 80-85% depends on demand and expansions due around end-FY27.
